title: PosterBench calibration cannot drift through an optimization loop that does not consume PosterBench
dead_end_scope: The standalone claim that AutoDesign's recursive optimization can directly overfit or reward-hack PosterBench itself, causing PosterBench's human-preference calibration to drift during the released optimization loop.

counter_explanation.statement: AutoDesign explicitly separates the optimization-time evaluator R_meta from the frozen PosterBench protocol. R_meta is built before autonomous optimization and supplies rollout scores and train/dev acceptance feedback. PosterBench is a distinct frozen protocol used for completed-system comparison and the system-blind human-alignment study. Because PosterBench scores are not consumed by the released update proposal or acceptance transition, PosterBench itself has no causal write path into the optimization trajectory.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: Holding R_meta, train/dev tasks, optimizer inputs, proposed updates, and randomness fixed, changing only PosterBench scores or PosterBench membership cannot change the released AutoDesign harness-update trajectory. It can change only the final reported benchmark comparison. Any optimizer-induced validity failure must therefore occur in R_meta, the repeatedly reused dev gate, or another selection-facing signal, not in report-only PosterBench.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: Evaluation can be adaptively overfit only through a selection-facing feedback path; a frozen report-only benchmark is trajectory-invariant by construction.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Search for optimization-time evaluator or validation signals that are actually consumed by update proposal, gating, rollback, or persistent optimization history. Do not use final report-only PosterBench calibration as evidence of optimizer feedback. A valid next object must identify the selection-facing signal and then survive adaptive-validation/reusable-holdout reductions.
counter_explanation.scope: AutoDesign arXiv:2608.13560v1, especially the outer-loop definition distinguishing fixed R_meta from the separate frozen PosterBench final evaluation protocol.
counter_explanation.structural_witness: The paper states that R_meta remains fixed during autonomous optimization and is used to score rollouts; it separately states that this optimization-time evaluator is distinct from the frozen PosterBench protocol used for final system comparison. PosterBench therefore has no update-edge in the released outer-loop equations.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: PosterBench is the optimization evaluator: contradicted by the paper's explicit R_meta-versus-PosterBench distinction.
PosterBench controls update acceptance: the released acceptance equation uses J_train and J_dev under R_meta, not PosterBench.
Human-blind preference enters the optimization loop: the human study is reported as final independent evaluation, not an update signal.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only if first-party evidence shows PosterBench or an equivalent frozen final benchmark score is actually consumed by a later AutoDesign update, gate, rollback, synthesis, or selection transition. Merely evaluating more checkpoints on PosterBench after optimization is insufficient.

scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: PosterBench-human calibration is useful external evidence but cannot by itself diagnose optimizer-induced benchmark overfitting in AutoDesign because PosterBench is outside the released update path.
